title: Why Gas Prices Just Hit a Record (The 21-Mile Choke Point)
alts: Gas Prices Explained: One 21-Mile Strait Controls Your Tank
Why Gas Goes Up Like a Rocket and Down Like a Feather
line1: Why are gas prices so high? A fifth of the world's oil normally squeezes through a 21-mile strait, and in 2026 traffic there fell 95%.
summary: Dave pays $67 for one tank as the US average hits about $4.48, the highest September ever, and diesel breaks its all-time record above $6. We follow one barrel of oil from the 2026 Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz to Dave's receipt: Brent above $100, what's inside a gallon of gas, why prices rise like a rocket and fall like a feather, the 1973 oil embargo, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve at its lowest since 1983, and who wins and loses.
